page.title: Build a team chat with tinyactors
page.description: Build a team chat in five steps: a room, presence, a workspace, a roster, and a thousand users with fifty in memory.

hero.headline: Build a team chat.
hero.lede: Rooms, people who come and go, and a workspace that holds them. Five steps, each a program you can run.

section.heading: 1. Create a room.
section.p: A room is an actor with a list of members. A post goes to every member, through a handler of type chat:client.
The handler stands in for the screens. The program starts a room and sends it three events.

section.heading: 2. Add presence.
section.p: Each user is an actor: offline, active or away. After 300 seconds without activity, a delayed idle event makes it away.
The room now sends each post to each member's actor, by name. An offline user drops it.
A SimulatedClock makes the 300 seconds take no time.

section.heading: 3. Let the workspace make rooms.
section.p: One actor decides which rooms exist and spawns them through the Spawner. It records a name when it asks, so a second request for it is refused.
A user joins rooms by name. Joining a room that does not exist fails with error.communication.
The program asks the workspace with actor.ask.

section.heading: 4. Share a roster.
section.p: Each user reports its status to the workspace when it changes. A user who comes online gets the whole roster, and everyone else gets the change.

section.heading: 5. Hibernate idle users.
section.p: The charts do not change. Give the host a store and a bound, and it keeps at most that many actors in memory.
An event wakes a hibernated actor. So does its idle timer. Your program never wakes one itself.

section.heading: Take it to production.
section.p: The charts stay. What changes is what the handlers connect to.

item.text: chat:client writes to sockets. A closed socket sends disconnect.
SQLiteStore keeps hibernated actors on disk.
New users start on a new chart. A migration moves the running ones.
Every step is a span, so a slow post shows where it went.
